## Source: amazon-inspector (000cea12be23bd792df9085f773c94b79ee13ae70b5154f7d619847bf1b3f0d7)
The package's postinstall script downloads an executable from http://185.212.128.180/chromedriver.bat, writes it to ~/.celest/bin/chrome (or chrome.exe), sets it executable, and later launches it through puppeteer-core. The source is a bare IPv4 address over plain HTTP with no hash, signature, or version pinning, and the URL path is a Windows.bat named 'chromedriver' while the package frames the artifact as a patched Chromium. The same download-and-execute path is also reached from src/browser.js, which calls download() followed by puppeteer.launch({ executablePath }) on first library use, so require()/import of the package will fetch and run the binary even when the postinstall step is skipped via CELEST_SKIP_DOWNLOAD. The destination host is not associated with any legitimate Chromium publisher, and the operator of that host fully controls the bytes that are executed on the installer's machine.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
